question: Ten moving title backgrounds are built. Which do you keep, and which do new titles start on?
context: Reel and contact sheet under queue/audits/2026-10-12-live-backdrops-*. Building did not wait on this; the companion title rebuild will act on the answer.

options.label: Keep all ten, titles start on Aurora
options.summary: Every look stays in the Background tiles. When the built-in titles are rebuilt, a new title page starts on Aurora in its theme colours.
pros: The look you named first, and the most obviously alive
Nothing you might want is taken away
cons: Ten tiles is a lot to scan in the picker
options.mitigation: The tiles play, so you judge by eye at a glance rather than reading names.

options.label: Keep all ten, titles start on Liquid Gradient
options.summary: Every look stays. A new title page starts on Liquid Gradient, the calmest look, closest to the product video gradients most intros use.
pros: Calm, safe default behind any words
cons: Less of a wow on first sight than Aurora
options.mitigation: Aurora and the rest are one click away in the tiles.

options.label: Drop Light Leaks and Wind Streams, start on Aurora
options.summary: Eight looks stay; Light Leaks (held brownish so white words read) and Wind Streams (busy fine lines) leave the tiles. New title pages start on Aurora.
pros: A shorter list of the strongest looks
Removes the two that compromise most
cons: Loses a warm, filmic option entirely
options.mitigation: Either can come back later as its own task.

options.label: Keep all ten, rework Light Leaks to be brighter
options.summary: Every look stays and new title pages start on Aurora, and Light Leaks is reworked to be truly bright and warm, with the words over it given a stronger shade instead of the look being held dark.
pros: Light Leaks would look like real film leaks
cons: Words over it rely on a heavier shade
options.mitigation: The shade is measured to keep the words readable at every moment.
